notes.title: Winter Survival just got Major Update! 👀
notes.notes: [h1]Hey, survivors! ❄️[/h1][p][/p][p]Welcome to another [b]major update for Winter Survival[/b]. After a series of episodes where we’ve been teasing a little bit of what we’ve been working on for the past few months, it's high time to finally share it with our beloved community. We’ve rolled out a brand-new update packed with [b]reworks, improvements, and bug fixes[/b] to make your survival experience smoother, more balanced, and more immersive. Stick with me till the end, as we might have something that you’d definitely want to keep an eye out on 👀[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/f99dab292d8314b59a37f55c8b610a199e6d700b.png"][/img][/p][p]Due to fundamental changes in the game’s questline and various other data, we regret to announce that old save files are no longer compatible after this update (16th of September, 2025). [/p][p]If you want to continue your old playthrough, please make sure to use the “legacy” branch.[/p][p]More information can be found in the pinned thread via Steam discussions. You can also proceed directly to that thread by clicking [url="https://steamcommunity.com/app/1394960/discussions/0/572642335441059103/"]this link[/url] If you want to continue your playthrough on your old saves, it might be worth to have some sort of a backup of your old saves. Check [url="https://steamcommunity.com/app/1394960/discussions/0/572642335441059300/"]this link[/url] to see how to do it properly. [/p][p]When starting the game, there is a new screen that will open up - Shader Compilation Screen. This will attempt to precompile all shaders in the game for your hardware so that the game can run smoothly when being played, rather than compiling them on the go (which can be a cause of hitches). The visual representation of this widget is temporary.[/p][p]The compilation of shaders is very resource-intensive on the hardware, so if you are getting repeated crashes on this, please let us know your computer specs here or on Discord - CPU, GPU, and Hard Disk that you are installing the game on as it can help us remove these issues before full release of the game, or finding alternative solutions for these cases. Restarting a game may help with some of the issues.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Major Reworks & Improvements 🛠️[/b][/h2][p][i][b]Note:[/b] These patch notes highlight a selection of fixes and improvements. They are not exhaustive. Many systems were fully reworked (such as Sanity, Status Cards, Torch, and more), and those broader changes are not listed here as simple bug fixes.[/i][/p][p][/p][h3][b]New Easy Difficulty Level[/b][/h3][p]A new [i]Newcomer[/i] difficulty setting has been added to make the game more approachable for players seeking a lighter challenge. This mode lowers survival demands (hunger, thirst, tiredness) and combat intensity, which should help you experience the Story Mode and explore the Survival Mode.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Sanity Rework [/b][/h3][p]The Sanity System was visually updated and expanded with late-game mechanics, offering clearer feedback and a greater impact on gameplay at higher Adaptation levels.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Status Card Rework[/b][/h3][p]Status cards were redesigned for clarity and now provide more information about the environment and wilderness events, making it easier to prepare for what’s coming in the wild.[/p][h3][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1394960/view/569255906735293427"][/dynamiclink][b]Torch Rework [/b][/h3][p]The torch was integrated into the new combat system and can now be used as a weapon. Controls are smoother, durability is better balanced, and now you can block with it. It is still primarily used as a tool to scare away wolves when lit, rather than as a brute force weapon.[/p][h3][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1394960/view/525343813853513095"][/dynamiclink][b]Crafting UI Rework[/b] [/h3][p]The crafting interface was redesigned with cleaner navigation, now providing players with more information about crafted items for a clearer experience and less waste. We've talked a little bit about it in our previous announcement, so you can freely check this one out here:[/p][h3][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1394960/view/525346984576421315"][/dynamiclink][/h3][h3][b]Trolley Damage Rework[/b][/h3][p]The Trolley breaking up mechanic was adjusted to provide balanced and fair damage mechanics.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Bear Event Rework[/b][/h3][p]We completely reworked the Bear Wilderness Event. Now, the interaction with it is more intuitive for the player. You can check [b]The Road to Survival Just Got Smoother [/b]announcement [/p][p][/p][h3][b]Graphic Improvements [/b][/h3][p]The resource graphics have been fully overhauled with updated models, textures, and a consistent PBR workflow, including redesigned animal models with improved fur and updated foliage and hard surface assets. The rendering system has been enhanced with extensive exposure adjustments, and alternative versions of resources have been added to match different biomes. Overall, existing content has been polished to meet the quality standards of a full release.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Performance Improvements[/b][/h3][p]High settings now run efficiently on RTX 2060 and higher graphics cards. Major optimization of memory consumption for improved stability and performance. Added support for FSR, TSR, and DLSS technologies for enhanced upscaling and performance. Optimized water systems for oceans and rivers to improve performance and visual fidelity. notes.title: Into the Unknown (ACT III Preview)
notes.notes:
[h1]Hey, survivors! [/h1][p]The cold has carried you far.

From the first desperate scramble to find shelter, through each fire lit against the dark, you’ve fought tooth and nail to stay alive. ACT II ended with steel, grit, and courage – the ride that tore through the night and shattered the barrier standing in your way. The gates fell, but beyond them… a land unknown awaits.[/p][p align="center"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/5fd934a1956167d47388366e3f1dbec4486cc1e1.png"][/img][/p][h2][b]ACT III – A New Land, A New Threat 🏝️[/b][/h2][p]Winter Survival’s third act will bring the toughest challenges yet, closing the story while expanding survival in new directions. With the gate behind you, you’ll step into a new environment unlike anything seen before.[/p][p align="center"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/5c8a74a36ecc29268a386cefcb1ac211f22e5ec8.gif"][/img][/p][p]Here, snow begins to give way to something else – unstable ground, murky water, and an atmosphere heavy with tension. Paths twist and vanish into mist. Landmarks shift. What once felt solid no longer is. Nature has changed its shape, and so too must your instincts if you’re to endure.[/p][p align="center"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/828c7b5fe084a426767f9671db032a1558c30e12.jpg"][/img][/p][p]But the land doesn’t just look different – it [i]behaves[/i] differently. What stood tall can fall without warning, cutting off routes, reshaping trails, and forcing you to adapt quickly. Survival here means more than warmth and food – it means awareness, timing, and caution at every step.[/p][p align="center"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/606b141a52a89df65bb2a9d90e2dba07006df54d.jpg"][/img][/p][h2][b]New Gameplay Challenges[/b][/h2][p]With this act, the ways you interact with the world expand once again.[/p][list][*][p][b]New environment:[/b] The swampy region introduces terrain where movement itself becomes a risk.[/p][/*][*][p][b]More Dynamic Events:[/b] The forest no longer feels still. Trees collapse unexpectedly, or maybe someone is “helping” them to collapse?[/p][/*][*][p][b]Evolving survival:[/b] Resources grow scarcer, choices harder. Familiar tools won’t always give the same comfort they once did.[/p][/*][/list][h2][b]Closing the Story[/b][/h2][p]ACT III doesn’t just bring new dangers. It brings answers. The story that has followed you since your first waking breath in this frozen nightmare begins to tie together. Every decision you’ve made across ACT I and II will resonate louder as you approach the conclusion.[/p][p align="center"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/d3e126ed29bb95f079b298fb3f888979bed8885a.jpg"][/img][/p][p]The world will no longer remain silent about what has happened here. The shadows that haunted you, the figures glimpsed in firelight, the whispers carried by the wind – ACT III brings them forward. Some questions will be answered. Some will be left to linger. But your journey will find its end.[/p][h2][b]The Road Ahead[/b][/h2][p]ACT III is more than just a continuation – it’s the culmination. A new region to test your survival. New challenges that break the patterns you’ve grown used to. And the final steps in a story that has carried you from frostbitten nights to gates torn open by fire. You’ve come this far. But what lies ahead will demand more than ever before. Keep your fire burning. The end is near.[/p][p align="center"][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/1394960/Winter_Survival/"][/dynamiclink][/p][p][i]~Sewek[/i][/p]

notes.title: The Road to Survival Just Got Smoother 🛤️👌
notes.notes:
[h1]Hey, survivors![/h1]

It’s time for another round of updates to be rolled out in Act III. This devlog focuses on technical improvements that influence gameplay, including crafting UI, building system, and animal tracking events.

[h2]Crafting with clarity - UI Improvements 🧩✨[/h2]

Crafting is no longer a walk in the dark. We've reworked the crafting UI to give you insight into what you’re making and how it works.

[list]
[*] You’ll now see what effects your crafted item will remove, and how completely.
For example, do you want to stabilize a broken leg? You’ll know right away that the leg stabilizer removes the twisted ankle effect 100%.
[*] We’ve also removed the energy cost associated with crafting. Finally, no more second-guessing whether you can afford to craft in the middle of a blizzard. Now, if you have the materials, you can build it.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/49a4d9f9237a5052ce5895cd24d5043e030decce.jpg[/img]

[h2]Fixing Shelter - Upgrade of the Building System 🔨🏠[/h2]

The shelter building system just got a visual communication upgrade. No more hovering over buildings to guess if something’s off. Now, Instinct Mode visual cues tell you instantly if repairs are needed.
[list]
[*] We’ve improved how damage and destruction are shown on structures.[/list]
With better visual feedback, you will know when you need to fix your place to stay.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/362bbf6d5e8035b27019b14133ef749f1c66f16f.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/bb464dc2b96c56f53b8a27325cc30a0bfe4a1643.jpg[/img]

Let’s take a look at tracking the bear. Previously, trailing wildlife was more guesswork than strategy, so we’ve rebuilt the tracking event to let you take control. 
[list]
[*] Also, the bear tracks are easier to spot, making it possible to simply avoid a deadly encounter altogether. We also revised their locations on the map.
[*] We’ve upgraded a meat pile that makes the bear sleep.
[/list]
Each of these changes was designed to make key systems more intuitive, provide better information up front, and reduce unnecessary friction during play.

notes.title: The Voice That Still Echoes: A New Chapter Begins in Winter Survival
notes.notes:
[h3][b]Hey, survivors![/b][/h3][p]We’ve been hard at work on some updates, and just as promised, it’s time to check what’s waiting up ahead in the upcoming Act III. This devlog is our next checkpoint.[/p][p]And as always, we’re not steering alone. Your feedback shapes the path ahead as well. Let’s take a ride through the latest changes.[/p][p]In this devlog, we’re introducing a set of improvements that will have a significant impact on interacting with the game and its core gameplay systems.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/5cebba4525a0bba797799d1316b623d7fdb139b9.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3][b]First stop: The Status Rework[/b][/h3][p]We’ve retouched the Status Tab to keep you better prepared. It’s now split into two clear sections: [b]Health[/b] and the brand-new [b]Environment Tab[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][b]Health:[/b] you’ll now have better visibility of perks, symptoms, mental state, and status effects, as well as the stench determining how the animals can detect you.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/db5a5365e9b09c2bd4ac186be5e4ee2523c695b6.jpg"][/img][/p][p]Inside the [b]Environment Tab,[/b] you’ll find:[/p][list][*][p][b]Compass Markers:[/b] every marker you’ve dropped across the wilderness is now easy to track.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Wilderness Events:[/b] all unlocked events are listed and clickable, taking you straight to your journal. Some are tied to what you do in the wild: sleeping, cooking, or moving through dangerous areas, and the world reacts adaptively.[/p][/*][/list][p]A small shift on the surface, but one that sharpens your decision-making when the cold hits hard.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/6c8808b991117c6d7b492fc67ff1c9611070f464.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]Next up: Trolley 2.0[/b][/h3][p]The trolley is more than just a ride. So we gave it the attention it deserved. The old damage system felt clunky and sometimes unclear, so we rebuilt it from the wheels up.[/p][p]We polished a more comfortable ride and smoother track switching. Now, when your trolley breaks down, you’ll get instant visual feedback not only showing that something’s wrong, but also how bad the damage is. This new system is designed to improve clarity. In the heat of survival, you don’t want to waste time, and now, you won’t have to.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/95901b246d7ed939d1efd99f2768233c851f0e83.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]Story Mode: Where the journey begins[/b][/h3][p]Shaping a unique playthrough in the mysterious Story Mode is perfect for those who want more than just the fight to stay alive. From the beginning, your path is shaped by constant movement. For newcomers, it’s a great way to get familiar with the genre without being thrown into the deep end. For seasoned survivalists, it offers clever twists on core mechanics and a compelling narrative that keeps you engaged.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/16f59060b4f4a84c7c90f9074ffe0efd0af409eb.gif"][/img][/p][h3][i][b]Winter’s Tale #1 — The Voice That Still Echoes[/b][/i][/h3][p]No one is born a hero. But when the world turns upside down, you don’t get to choose. Especially not Danny, just an engineer with a head full of unfinished business, who only wanted to spend a few quiet days in the forest before his life changed forever.[/p][p]He left Sarah behind: tired, disappointed, yet still holding on to the hope that he might finally grow up. She is pregnant and has given him one last chance. As he walked out the door, she said just one thing, calmly, without reproach: [i]“Honey, I’m waiting.”[/i][/p][p]The trip was meant to clear their heads. Just Danny, Joel, and Mike, best friends, out for a few quiet days in the frozen forest. For a while, everything felt almost normal. Then the blizzard came, and things began to fall apart.[/p][p]He’s woken by Joel’s scream and the sound of branches snapping, followed by a bear’s roar nearby and, somewhere beyond, the howling of wolves. Mike is gone, lost in the chaos. The snow has already buried their tracks before they can make sense of what happened.[/p][p]From that moment, the nightmare begins. Cold seeps into bone, fear locks the body in place, and every step becomes a risk. But this is also where the story starts. [i]Winter Survival[/i] isn’t about survival in the traditional sense; it’s about adaptation, about how far you’re willing to change just to stay alive.[/p][p]Narrative Story Mode guides you carefully, step by step. It shows you how to survive the first attack, how to build a shelter, and how to make it through the night in a cave that might not be empty.[/p][p]This isn’t a story about heroes. It’s a story about those who aren’t ready to give up.
 And about a voice that still echoes, long after everything else has frozen:[/p][p][b]“Honey, I’m waiting.”[/b][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/676b1bd5100f4d885f9c9749963875784f895a78.jpg"][/img][/p][h3][b]The road ahead[/b][/h3][p]Thanks for riding with us in this devlog and shaping the game alongside us. Got feedback, questions, or wild theories? Drop them in the comments; most of what you see here started with a message from you, Survivors.[/p][p]Stay sharp. Stay warm.
And don’t let the trolley freeze over.[/p][p]~ Kinia[/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Torch Rework 🔥, further optimization, balancing, and more!
notes.notes:
[h1]Hey, Survivors! ❄️[/h1]

As promised in our last announcement (check it out [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1394960/view/525342544971695800][here][/url] if you haven’t yet), it’s high time for the next part of our development sneak peek series, where we take a closer look at what we’ve been cooking up for you over the past few months.

We've been listening closely to your feedback and working hard behind the scenes to deliver an update that not only polishes core systems, but also introduces much-anticipated changes to balance and optimization. Let’s break down each change coming to the game alongside ACT III 👇

[h2]Torch Rework – More Than Just a Light Source 🔥[/h2]

Your torch is no longer just for visibility – it’s now a viable defensive tool in combat. Up until now, it’s been useful for fending off wolves or lighting your path through dark caves and nighttime exploration (seriously, what are you doing wandering the wilderness at night?).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/2d5b3f091bd4878757e3dc7134fa06817c4b2d42.gif[/img]

With the reworked torch, players will now be able to block incoming attacks, making it a vital part of your survival kit. And when the fuel runs out? You’re not defenseless – you’ll still have a burnt-out stick to use as a makeshift melee weapon.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/1fb67491b6e8f599a5154ee5c97c8c199f4a3520.gif[/img]

Just to be clear though – don’t count on it for hunting wolves. It’s a last resort, not a deadly weapon.

[h2]Symptom Tree Overhaul 🧠[/h2]

The Symptom Tree is getting a visual overhaul to make it clearer, more intuitive, and easier to understand. But we’re not stopping there.

With this update, you’ll also be able to stack the same symptom multiple times. That means symptoms can linger longer and become more severe, depending on the path you choose. It’s all up to you – and your decisions will matter more than ever.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/55f317399850fe31a6595d8b219563e5b1e997a0.jpg[/img]

[h2]Optimized Wind for Better Performance 💨[/h2]

We know many of you want to experience the brutal winter landscapes of Winter Survival without compromising performance. We’ve seen your comments and reviews regarding optimization, and we’re constantly looking for new ways to improve it.

This brings us to the new Wind system. While it might not sound like a big change, it’s been designed with performance in mind, and it will help boost frame rates for many players. Once the update is live, we’d love to hear your thoughts and feedback on how it’s performing for you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/22878a4bc298dd72a311cb418842e5caf469be20.gif[/img]

[h2]Weather System Rebalance 🌧️[/h2]

You spoke, and we listened. The Weather System will be rebalanced to address key issues raised by the community. Don’t worry – it’s still going to be tough out there. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/388095de37a38f237e8910572202629eb8a6716f.gif[/img]

[h2]Holding block no longer drains stamina? 🤯[/h2]

This might be the biggest change coming to Winter Survival (at least for me!). And yes – you read that right – holding block will no longer drain stamina. That means you can hold your defensive stance without watching your stamina bar melt away. Combined with the new torch mechanics, you’ll have way more flexibility in how you approach every encounter. 

[h2]Stay Up-to-Date 📰[/h2]

That’s it for now! As always, thank you for your continued support and feedback. Drop us a comment below with your thoughts on the upcoming features, and let us know if there’s anything else you’d like to see added to Winter Survival.

As for the next announcement, you can expect it mid-June. We’ll be shifting our focus toward Story Mode, and sharing more about what’s coming in ACT III. Stay sane – and until the next devlog! 👋

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1394960/Winter_Survival/

[i]~Sewek[/i]

notes.title: Let's talk about the reworked combat system in Winter Survival 👊

[h1]Hey, Survivors! ❄️[/h1]

Welcome into the first announcement in 2025. How was your holiday? I hope you spend some time defeating your never-ending gaming backlog and you’re right now ready to face the challenges of a New Year. 

As Winter Survival continues its journey through development, it’s time to focus on yet another core mechanic that we’ve managed to completely rework some time ago which is   combat. 🪓 

Our team has been hard at work overhauling how you face off against threats, so that every encounter feels more immersive, tactical, and rewarding. Let’s see what has been changed, shall we?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/16b3ac1d299f74fe757d1ff65f75d8d4c52f7369.jpg[/img]

[h2]Refining the Core Combat Experience 🧠[/h2]

Since day one, our aim has been to capture the raw intensity of surviving in the cold wild. With your feedback in mind, we’ve reevaluated how combat functions. We wanted it to be challenging yet fair, empowering you to find multiple ways to defend yourself and make meaningful decisions in the heat of the moment.

[h3]Block Attacks 🛡️[/h3]

Gone are the days of just swinging wildly to keep enemies at bay. We’ve introduced a block mechanic that allows you to raise your guard and mitigate incoming damage. While you won’t entirely avoid harm, timing your blocks just right can tip the scales in your favor. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/154ddb64eb7d11b41b8cf3a67164416a5d49bb6e.gif[/img]

[h3]Using Your Axe for Defense 🪓[/h3]

Your trusty axe isn’t just for chopping wood anymore — it can also help you block and parry enemy attacks. We heard from many players who wanted more versatility in their gear loadout, so we made sure your go-to tool could double up as a defensive option. It may be heavier and slower to maneuver than a spear, but its stopping power is unmatched.

notes.title: Revisiting the Game Modes in Winter Survival 👀
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/64e82695b3b9395a19b8e2d3d00fa11c2fec7ac1.gif[/img]

[h1]Hello, survivors! ❄️[/h1]

It’s hard to believe it’s already been eight months since Winter Survival launched into Early Access. It feels like yesterday I was writing the launch announcement and we’re already slowly but surely approaching 2025. Today, we want to take a moment to revisit the game modes that make Winter Survival a diverse and compelling experience, providing something for everyone — from newcomers to the most hardcore survivalists.

We’ll also touch on what makes each mode unique and why you should explore them if you haven’t already. Plus, a quick update on what’s ahead for the story! So, without further ado, let’s roll!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/082429f2f06bb3cbd531ff71be2e3e541d94696f.jpg[/img]

[h2]Search for your missing friends in Story Mode ⛰️[/h2]

If you’re new to Winter Survival or simply prefer a more guided introduction to its mechanics, [b]Story Mode is where your adventure should start[/b]. In this mode, you step into the shoes of Danny, a determined yet rookie survivalist who is desperately seeking for his missing friends in the unforgiving wilderness.

Story Mode isn’t just about the destination — it’s about the journey. As Danny, you’ll gradually learn and master all of the essential survival mechanics.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/18d8487a3a13351c0b49f8bceceb241a00874942.jpg[/img]

This mode is designed for players who want a more deliberate pace while immersing themselves in the narrative. It’s perfect for those looking to balance storytelling with survival gameplay. Currently, Story Mode includes ACT I and II but we’re still hard at work on Act III of Danny’s story, where even more challenges and revelations await. 

Unfortunately, I cannot share much right now, so stay tuned for more information coming soon! And let’s not forget that ACT I and II have gone through a rework some time ago, so for those who completed it already, it might be a really good idea to replay it once again. 

[h2]Brave the elements and survive in Survival Mode 🐻[/h2]

For those seeking freedom, creativity, and most importantly more challenging experience –  [b]Survival Mode should be your go-to mode when you first launch the game[/b]. In this open-ended sandbox, the primary goal is simple: stay alive as long as you can. 

How you achieve that is entirely up to you. Build your cozy base, master resource gathering, and experiment with different strategies for long-term survival. With no fixed narrative, this mode encourages exploration and player-driven goals. Want to see how big your base can grow? Curious about the limits of your crafting skills? Survival Mode is where you can truly make the wilderness your own.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/8f4989c45a535c973958bc1435a92ba4bf5fc4e0.jpg[/img]

[h2]Climb up the ladder in Cold Wave Mode 🥶[/h2]

Are you a Winter Survival veteran looking for the ultimate test of skill? Enter Cold Wave, a mode specifically designed for hardcore players who have mastered every nuance of survival.
This is where the stakes are raised to a whole new level. 

In the Cold Wave, your mission is not just to survive but to thrive under extreme conditions. The cold is relentless, the resources are scarce, and your endurance will be pushed to the limit. For those who thrive on competition and relentless difficulty, Cold Wave offers unmatched intensity. Prove your mettle, climb the ranks, and become the best survivalist out there. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/150587570c10d4c9fe7f1eed55d085d9f7f59c8e.jpg[/img]

[h2]Stay up-to-date 📰[/h2]

notes.title: Current state of the game and future plans for Winter Survival🐻
notes.notes:
[h1]Hey, survivors! ❄️[/h1]

As Winter is slowly but surely approaching, I thought it’s gonna be the perfect time to finally share with you some inside info about the current state of the game and what our future plans are. It’s gonna be a fully transparent statement from our side, so I highly encourage you to read it till the end. I will divide the announcement into separate sections for easier and more convenient navigation, because I feel it might be a pretty long devlog. So, let’s not waste more time, and jump straight into it, shall we? 👇

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/9c9cb26659948bb87e778b3f645a7aa3d73bbbc3.jpg[/img]

[h2]Current State of the Game 📈[/h2]

Currently, Winter Survival has three different game modes to offer: [b]Story Mode, Survival, and Cold Wave[/b]. Each one of them gives you a whole new experience and totally different approach to the game. For example in Story Mode you will [b]experience the story of Danny and his missing friends[/b] while learning step by step all of the necessary survival mechanics like building, hunting, and simply staying alive. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/92340ee9fcb9cf8c4cd18c70a612720455c76609.jpg[/img]

Right now there are two acts available for you to try and for those of you who have already experienced it, I highly suggest you to go through it once again, because [b]a lot has changed[/b] since the initial release into Early Access back in March 2024. And obviously that’s not all that we have to offer, but we’ll come back to it later on in this announcement. 

Apart from the Story Mode, there are also survival and cold wave modes available. Survival offers you the opportunity to test your skills and master them to the perfection while staying alive as long as you can. Cold Wave however is aimed for the seasonal experts who have already learnt the ins and outs of the game and are looking to test their knowledge against the others. The idea is quite simple – the longer you stay alive while facing the ever-worsening weather, the higher your score will be. But the question is – how much are you willing to sacrifice to climb up the ladder? 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/64e82695b3b9395a19b8e2d3d00fa11c2fec7ac1.gif[/img]

[h3]Fixes and QoL improvements 🪱[/h3]

Obviously, content is one thing and fixing the game is the other, and we’re fully aware that we didn’t have quite the start we wanted and there were many of you who have experienced game breaking issues. But, thanks to your help and support we’ve managed to track most of those pesky bugs and problems. Since our EA launch back in March, we’ve managed to fix approximately five hundred bugs and adjust a plethora of different things to balance the game according to your feedback. 

The icing on the cake is dozens of changes and general improvements that made their way into the game. To fully witness what we’ve managed to do, check our updated road map below. Rest assured, we’re still tracking your reports in Steam discussions, announcements, and on our discord server, so don’t hesitate and keep those comments coming, folks! 👍

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/0c79302ade59f589756c4eaada5c96a2149071f7.jpg[/img]

[h2]What future holds for Winter Survival 🤔?[/h2]

Alrighty, since we’ve managed to cover the current state of the game, now it’s gonna be the high time to share some inside info about the future plans for the game. Let’s roll! 

[h3]We’re working on ACT III 🔥[/h3]

Yes, you’ve heard that right! Currently we have a dedicated team that is focusing purely on bringing you the much anticipated ACT III for the story mode. Most of our efforts are put into the whole ACT III quest chain while working on brand-new features of which I cannot speak as of yet. It’s still quite a long journey till the end, but looking back in time we want to make sure that we deliver the best quality product possible to simply avoid any form of disappointment from your side. 

Basically from now on we want to make sure that we're more than happy with the quality of the final product and only after that release it to you. No worries tho – the paratrooper makes sure that we work hard on a daily basis. Don't make him angry. You won't like him when he's angry! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/fbe2a12f85924142796c0a61aa824e5417899674.jpg[/img]

[h3]Updates are on its way 👀[/h3]

I hope you’re still with me, because I promise that is the last thing we need to talk about. We understand that there are still issues, bugs, or problems – you name it – that we need to deal with. Having said that, till the end of a year you can expect two more game updates coming your way. We still do not have the exact date of the release, but as soon as I get that out from our producers, I’m gonna share that with you. 

[h2]Stay up-to-date 📰[/h2]

Unfortunately, all good things come to an end. Right now, we’re waiting for your comments, so if you have any questions, suggestions, or simply would like to share your opinion with us, make sure to leave your answer in the comment section below. I’ll make sure to keep you folks updated on a regular basis regarding the progress we’ve made so far, but for now until the next devlog! 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1394960/Winter_Survival/

[i]~Sewek[/i]

notes.title: ACT II and Cold Wave are available now! 🔥
notes.notes:
[h1]Hey, Survivors! ❄️[/h1]

We are incredibly excited to announce that ACT II of Winter Survival is now live, along with our brand-new game mode, Cold Wave! Apart from that there are a plethora of bug fixes, improvements, and changes to the game, so in other words – a lot of stuff to delve into. We've been working hard to bring you these updates, and we can't wait for you to dive in and experience all the new content and improvements. What say you if we kick the things off with a spicy teaser that showcases some of the changes that we’ve introduced? 

[previewyoutube=QdGx0dsI6yk;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]ACT II for Story Mode is here 👀[/h2]

In ACT II, you'll continue Danny's journey through the unforgiving winter landscape. This chapter is packed with new challenges, side quests, and storylines that deepen the mystery surrounding Danny's missing friends. Furthermore, we’ve made some significant improvements to ACT I as well, so even if you’ve experienced it before, we highly encourage you to jump back to it. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/b0dbe7ffe7bbbc46818283766a23268fea6ae68e.jpg[/img]

[h2]Test your limits in Cold Wave mode 📈[/h2]

Cold Wave mode is our new survival challenge designed for those who seek an even tougher test of their skills. In this mode, you'll face extreme weather conditions that push your survival strategies to the limit. The longer you survive, the higher your score – but beware, the cold is relentless and unforgiving. The ultimate question is – Will you risk your life in order to achieve a higher score? Dive in to check it out for yourself. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/7f15b77afe0e90b218c5243ffea2e05ccfb8f6db.jpg[/img]

[h2]Patch Notes for ACT II Update⚒️[/h2]

Keep in mind that the game is still in the Early Access, so the Update may affect your old saves. We recommend starting with a fresh save, but if you decide otherwise please remember to share with us any issues you may have.

[h3]New & Improvements[/h3]
[b]Act 2[/b] - next chapter of our Story, this time action revolves around Danny’s way to the Harbor, being stalked by foes and using some ingenious ways to make the trip easier for himself. 

[b]Cold Wave[/b] - New Game Mode - a new competitive game mode that allows you to test your survival skills against other players trying to climb the Leaderboards with each new run.

[b]New Side Quests:[/b]
[list]
[*] "Missing In Action" - Available in Story and Survival Game Modes.
[*] "Survivalist Instinct" - Only available in Story mode (Act I).
[*] "In Distress" - Only available in Story mode (Act II).
[*] "Truffle Pasta"  - Only available in Story mode (Act II).
[*] "Upgrade Your Shelter"  - Only available in Story mode (Act II).
[/list]

[b]Trolley Taking Damage Mechanic[/b] - It’s active in Survival Game Mode from the start and after you complete the main quest line in the Story Game Mode. The Trolley gets damaged over time and you need to look for the spare parts to keep it running.

[b]Axe Rework[/b] - Axe was reworked in the same new system as the Spear in the past update, it includes new animations, and the ability to block among other minor changes. It’s still a tool, not a weapon, so don’t get too eager to hunt Wolves with it but it can be used in an emergency.

[b]Trauma Rework[/b] - right now Trauma is more manageable without compromising its effects on the gameplay. Each effect is now timed and will deactivate after some time, which you can further decrease using various methods such as Comfort Foods etc.

[b]New Symptom: Panic Attack[/b] - Occasionally triggered while the symptom is active it requires you to return to a safe space to calm yourself down. Ignoring it will lead to bad consequences.

[b]New Symptom: Hypochondria[/b] - Makes you super attentive to your health and body functions. You start noticing some problems that aren’t really there.

[b]A new type of Bait for Large Prey[/b]- now you can craft specialized types of bait for larger animals like Deer.

[b]New Hardened Leather Clothing Set[/b] - a new set of clothes that will help you deal with harsh climate and animals - made from Wolf and Boar Skins.

[b]Compass Update[/b] - we added a couple of new features to the Compass, now you can name your markers, change their color and icon, and hide/destroy them at will.

[b]Different bleed values for various types of spears[/b] - there’s another reason to upgrade your spear, the better spear the better bleed value, which should make your combat and hunting easier.

[b]Tooltip rework[/b] - on Weapons and Tools now there should be more information about what you can do with each tool to make it clearer what is the purpose of each one of them.

[b]Knife Rework[/b] - Stone knife is now only used for Butchering, Bone Knife and above can be used for Skinning also.

[b]Rework Active and Passive Hunting[/b] - traps can break, and can return some resources when broken, fix that animals get freed instantly, etc. When placing items in the traps you should now be able to see if that item will work as a bait for any of the animals.

[b]Wolf Den Changes[/b] - almost all Wolves now are associated with a specific Wolf Den (before they weren't necessarily so), which means you can stop them from spawning by blocking the Den with a Blockade. The change also includes a completely new setup for Wolf Dens and Wolf Paths.

[b]Reworked Boar Truffle Hunting Mechanic[/b] - now it is easier to find and dig up truffles, also now it’s explained in the Story mode as a side-quest.

[b]Day/Night Cycle for Wolves and Weather[/b] - Night and Day are now differentiated with different amount of animals and different lifecycles during day/night. It should be more natural and nights should be more dangerous.

[b]Durability Damage on Clothes[/b] - Animals hitting you / biting you will now caused durability damage to clothes, meaning you might need to repair there a bit more often.

[b]Trolley[/b] - You can unmount trolley now also with the primary interaction. (E) by default. Trolley Upgrade: Big Storage. You can only have one storage upgrade on the trolley.

[b]Walkie Talkie[/b] - extra channel was added to the Story mode, to Walkie Talkie, to access the "Missing in Action" quest with it when it activates.

[b]Quest Tracking Rework[/b] - you can now only track one quest at a time, to make the UI less congested. When new quest pops up you can switch to the new quest by pressing X, or if there is nothing happening at the moment you can switch active tracking quest in Journal or by holding and releasing X for at least 1.5 seconds.
[list]
[*] Minor text updates to tutorials in the journal
[*] Stench can now be removed with Herbal Ointment.
[*] Added a recipe for fries.
[*] New Rabbit set up on the whole map.
[*] We completely reworked all stats related to the clothing Armour, Cold Protection, Wetness and Durability.
[*] Added 7 new misc items - a little bit more stuff to play with.
[*] More delusion animals were added across the map.
[*] Rearranged items in the Woodcutter’s Shelter in Act 1.
[*] We improved interactions with various items.
[*] In Story Mode, we added an axe-fighting tutorial in a cave under a Fallen Bridge and a spear-fighting tutorial near the start of Act II.
[*] A variety of resources placed throughout the world
[/list]
[h3]Balance[/h3]
[list]
[*] Cooked Wolf Meat now restores 22 hunger instead of 17 and has a description change to explain it's not supposed to be very edible. 
[*] New set up of Wolves both in Story and Endless
[*] Detection distances were altered on Deer and Wolf to make it a bit more predictable.
[*] Respawn time of Berry Bushes increased by 30%.

[*] Adjusted cargo loot tables to drop useful items and also trolley repair items + metal scraps
[*] Rabbits now respawn 10x faster when not killed but running away into a hole. [~20 in-game minutes]
[*] Wolf Den Blockade lasts 3 days instead of 2.
[*] It takes a shorter time for Boar to switch to searching after you hide in bushes.
[*] Now, you get branches from hitting the tree with an axe and log after you cut it.
[*] Armor calculations were changed to make different equipped clothes more valuable.
[*] Boar Light Attack damage reduced to 15 from 20.
[*] Boar Charge Attack damage increased to 30 from 20.
[*] Knockdown Attack of Wolf damage increased to 25 from 20.
[*] Removed boar and rabbit skin requirements from the Leather set, as a separate Hard Leather set now covers that requirement.
[*] Changed the number of branches dropped by trees, to provide more large branches more regularly.
[*] Deer will now wait until it is fully alerted to run away instead of at 50%.
[*] Thatch Bed now requires 2 ropes instead of 4.
[*] Thatch Windows and Slopes now require branches instead of large branches.
[*] Limited the energy-restoring qualities of food and drink.
[*] Switched the chance for Bear Attacking Shelter event on Survival Difficulty from 10% to 8%.
[*] Removed the speed reduction while the fever is active.
[*] Tweaked the amount of herbs required for Herbal Ointment. From 6 to 4.
[*] Set up the weight limit of the Tourist Pouch to 45.
[*] Changed the amount of Rabbit Skins needed to craft gloves from 6 to 2.
[*] Lowered nutritional values of wolf meat.
[*] Tweaked the progression of durability and its loss on knives.

[*] Now you can build a Stat Board from the start in Act 1. Using charcoal you can update it.
[*] New resources in the Fallen Bridge Cave.

notes.title: Game Update #10 - Combat and Trolley Rework
notes.notes:
[h2]New & Improvements[/h2]
[list]
[*] The Combat System has been reworked to offer a smoother and more dynamic experience when fighting using a spear. We also tweaked a lot of the damage values to be in-line with all these changes (see Balance section). 
[list]
[*] [b]Block[/b] has been added to combat allowing you to block attacks and mitigate damage. Blocking drains stamina. By default, hold the Right Mouse Button to block. 
[*] With the addition of Block, the [b]Throw[/b] mechanic has been tweaked, too. Use the V key to change to throwing and charge the throw with the Left Mouse Button as before. If you don’t like V as the key to do so, please remap it to a key of your liking in the Options.
[*] We got rid of the disorienting animation when impaling.
[*] Impaling can now [b]stun[/b] a target and the stunned state is now shown with a new Stunned marker on the animal. Dealing damage to the animal interrupts the stun.
[*] Wolves regained the ability to make the player [b]bleed[/b] with a bite attack!
[*] 15% change to apply a bleed effect with bite attack and 10% with knockdown on Survivalist difficulty.
[*] 10% change to apply a bleed effect with bite attack and 5% with knockdown on Explorer difficulty.
[/list][/list][list]
[*] Trolley has seen various improvements. Apart from various smaller fixes and tweaks, we reworked the Trolley Switches and Levers. You now [b]need a lever[/b] in order to activate a rail switch. Your previous switch settings have been reset with this update. Don’t worry though, you’ll find the levers close to the corresponding switch. The switches also have new visuals and they now show the direction they have been switched to.
[list]
[*] Trolley Torch Holder Upgrade - we added an additional upgrade to the Trolley, now you’ll have a source of light to ride through tunnels and in the night without the need to drain batteries on your flashlight..
[*] Trolley Storage Chest - another upgrade for the Trolley allowing you to have a mobile storage with [b]600 storage capacity[/b]. 
[*] Both upgrades are available in the Trolley Upgrade station in Endless mode upon reaching Adaptation level 25.
[/list]
[*] Compass and Compass Markers - now you can use compass markers to navigate around the environment. In Endless mode you can find the compass hidden in the environment, but in Story mode you’ll get it along with your other equipment in the backpack. Recipes for Compass Marker are available on Adaptation level 10 in Endless mode and immediately after finding the Compass in the Story. 
Wooden and Stone Markers can be crafted, so no matter where you are, the necessary resources should be easily available. Interact with the crafted and placed Compass Markers to select icons and colors that will indicate this location on your compass and make your navigation easier.
[*] Foxes - we added a new inhabitant to the Fox Glade which is the area in Endless that you can find behind a Trolley Gate. It may be hard to hunt it with a spear, but try to use the newly added Fox Snack to lure it into a trap. The Fox Snack is craftable on Adaptation level 9 in Endless mode.
[*] Added a schematic for a small Spear Holder and plugged it into the ending of False Dawn quest as well as first pickup of the item. Just in case you somehow manage to lose your basic spear holder.
[*] Added a schematic for a Stone Basket to the Adaptation System at Level 14 in Endless mode. As the name suggests, it allows you to store stones like the branch holders allow you to store branches.
[*] Empty alcohol bottles, wild flowers, broken boar tusks, leaky cans, old needles and rabbit feet made stackable.
[*] Improved the movement of the deer so it gets stuck less often in various world objects.

[/list]
[h2]Balance[/h2]
[list]
[*] Removed some Pete's Meat/Marko’s Beans on Trolley Station near the Hot Springs in the Story Act I area and the ruined house next to the bridge in the Story Act I area.
[*] Changed Rabbit’s rear detection distance to 750 (from 400).
[*] Changed Boar's rear detection distance to 700 (from 400).
[*] Changed Wolf's rear detection distance to 900 (from 400).
[*] Changed Deer’s rear detection distance to 1000 (from 400).
[*] Added wolf damage multiplier (120%) to the Survivalist difficulty.
[*] Adjusted the base damage on the Wolf’s bite from 5 to 10.
[*] Tweaked damage values for spears to better fit the new changes to combat. Please keep in mind that melee and thrown attacks offer a damage range and the actual damage depends on how much you charged that attacks.
[list]
[b]Sharpened Softwood Stick:[/b]
   Melee attack: 6-12
   Throw: 6-12
   Impale: 18
[b]Stone Tipped Spear:[/b]
   Melee attack: 10-18 
   Throw: 10-18
   Impale: 22
[b]Bone Tipped Spear:[/b]

   Throw: 14-26
   Impale: 30
[/list][/list]

[h2]Bugfixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Removed white border visual bug that was visible on some small icons.
[*] Added collision for the top part of Trolley.
[*] Fixed a bug with the amount of spears in Spear Holder.
[*] Fixed a bug with spears hitting Hiding Bushes.

[*] Fixed a bug with text not fitting in the booklet [Polish version only].

notes.title: Game Updates for the Next Two Weeks
notes.notes:
There will not be an update for the weekend today as we are working on larger updates for the end of next week and the following week. And we’d like to take a moment to give you a preview of the things that you can expect in terms of game updates over the next few weeks:

[b]Combat Rework[/b]
We have reworked the combat system quite significantly. The aim was to make combat smoother and slightly more dynamic. A good example is impaling with the spear. While it made some sense for your character to fall on his butt when impaling a wolf, the recovery time and looking sideways while falling turned out to be rather disorienting. 
We have thus reworked combat starting with the spear as it is currently the primary weapon. It is much smoother now, we added block, made tweaks to throwing and also stats.
Axe will be next. We never intended for the axe to be a weapon as such, but will now lean more in that direction.

[b]Trolley[/b]
Trolley is intended to take on a more important part of the game in the future, to become the basis of a mobile base. Apart of more fixes and tweaks, we are adding new functionality and mechanics to the trolley. Storage is one such thing so you can have mobile storage. We are even adding a holder for a torch to the trolley so you don’t have to relay on batteries when it gets dark (that’s why we increased torch duration in update #5).
There is also a mechanics coming where your trolley might suffer damage or break, along with new items to loot in order to perform the necessary repairs.

[b]Side Quests[/b]
Side quests are coming to the game and will either lead you to explore some special places or add new smaller locations. The idea is also for side quests to provide some unique rewards.
Side Quests will be available both in Story and Endless Mode.

[b]Survival Adventure[/b]
Speaking of Endless mode, we will rename it to Survival Adventure since the name Endless was a really bad choice. We also make it the first selection and Story the second one. In the future (after Story Act II) we will be adding more scenarios to this mode to have more interesting choices than Sickness and House scenarios. The idea here is to add scenarios that introduce players to different ways to survive and play the game.

[b]New Animals[/b]
We know we need a better variety when it comes to animals and we will be adding new ones, starting with foxes and mountain goats. While some will not have any special behaviours, some others will be more complex. Case in point the fox. It will react to wolves in the vicinity and the fox will be different when hunting it. You can’t trap it by placing a trap and put some bait in it. It’s a cunning animal and it will steal the bait. You will however be able to attract it with a special bait in your hand and for example place a trap in front of you.

Those are the highlights of what’s coming next week and the week after. Some smaller things not explicitly mentioned above build upon the changes to combat, so we can't release them before releasing the combat changes first. Hence the decision to roll them out later and in one update.

notes.title: Upcoming Game Updates
notes.notes:
With Easter coming up, we have to alter our schedule for game updates/patches for this and next week. We decided to skip the early week update we intended to do today and roll its content into a larger game update this Friday.

Similarly, there won’t be a smaller update right after Easter, but again a larger one at the end of next week.

Going forward, we also want to change how we approach updating the game. The idea is to have a [b]smaller game update[/b] early in the week (on a Tuesday in most cases) that will mostly focus on balancing and tweaks (unless there is a critical and time sensitive issue that requires fixing).

That smaller update will be followed a much [b]larger and more significant game update[/b] at the end of the week (on a Friday in most cases). These end of the week updates will contain new things and bigger changes and improvements. 

“Why the change?” you might wonder. We are not slowing down, quite the opposite actually as we are approaching the point where we will be adding new content to the game soon and this in turn requires more testing internally. It will be more efficient for us to split game updates into lighter ones early in the week and heavy ones at the end of a week since many of the bigger changes and fixes simply require more testing. So the bigger things get more time in testing throughout the week rather than just a couple of days.

I highly advise you to do so, since it covers every essential details you need to know about the sanity. Without further ado, let’s jump into it! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/a15dda826d2fb5c4f2ac4d3e8ccffeded2367f22.jpg[/img]

[h2]Psychosis Disorientation ⛰️[/h2]

Wolves might be a pain in the butt, but so are the imaginary parts of the environment. Let me give you an example – Imagine that you’re running away from the pack of wolves or a bear, and suddenly you see that a rock is blocking your way back home. Obviously with wolves being right behind, the adrenaline and stress will probably significantly lower your ability to think clearly, so you might end up in a dire situation. Oh… I forgot to mention that sometimes you might see some collectibles that might not really be there. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/b59f3b27ee931fe5a4d8d3aae96745b9aab59130.gif[/img]

[h2]Hunger Delusion 🍖[/h2]

Simply put – think about it as some sort of a mirage but with food. Imagine that you’re preparing yourself for a venture into the wilderness in order to search for some goodies. You double check your backpack to see if everything is in its place. After spending some time in the wild you’ve realized that your character is hungry, so you immediately set up a fire and cook a meal, right? Well, what if I tell you that the food you brought all the way up here was fake. That’s exactly what a hunger delusion is. Next time triple check, okay? 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/40ab39bca49c9f8e713f273f2d2627cb03ab9ec9.gif[/img]

[h2] Panic Attack 😱[/h2]

Well, I honestly don’t think I need to explain it much. Just like in real life too much stress, fear, or adrenaline might lead to a sudden panic attack – the state in which you’re not thinking clearly. In the worst cases it might even lead to fainting, which is exactly what this symptom does in Winter Survival. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/1075e110d5cfcf22aa1f9c42b6741b20620278a0.gif[/img]

[h2] Castle of Lies…🏰[/h2]

notes.title: Make your survival more challenging thanks to our Sanity System🧠
notes.notes:
[h1]Hey, survivors! ❄️[/h1]

Welcome to another development update for Winter Survival. I hope you had a fantastic time over the weekend and you’re ready to face the challenges awaiting you ahead. Speaking of challenges, in today’s devlog we’re gonna have a closer look into one of our features which will make your survival experience more unique and challenging. In other words - today’s devlog is [b]all about the sanity system[/b]. I just hope it won’t drive you mad after reading this 🙀

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/60242ecac924293c2f99b4b47ca4c99e2239cc06.jpg[/img]

Just before we jump into the nitty-gritty details, I just wanted to let you know that [b]Winter Survival is a part of the Steam Next Fest event[/b] which is already live. If you’re on a lookout for some challenging survival titles, Winter Survival is the game to go. What is more, if you still feel like you’d like to learn more about the demo and game itself, we’ll be [b]live streaming tomorrow at 7pm CET time[/b] over on Steam and our [url=https://www.twitch.tv/drago_entertainment]official twitch.tv account[/url]. If you have any questions for us, don’t hesitate and visit us tomorrow. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/fd60f1a983a10e9a8fb70ae7bb99ce4f1693f662.jpg[/img]

[h2]How does the Sanity System work? 🧠[/h2]

Alrighty, let’s start from the very beginning. In Winter Survival you as a player must take care of certain needs in order to stay alive. This includes: [b]hunger, thirst, temperature, energy, and your mind[/b]. What is more, during your gameplay you’ll face a variety of different debuffs that you will need to treat as well. Every time you neglect taking proper care of yourself, it’ll have a negative effect on your mind. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/b4ac62cd0ee0493f38ced3848cd70d7effd1948e.gif[/img]

How? Well, let me give you an example. Let’s assume that you have a bleeding debuff (because you weren’t careful enough and got bitten by a wolf, right?). As soon as the circle around your debuff fills, each time it affects your mind by a certain percentage. Once your brain fills 100%, the next time you go to sleep [b]the sanity system will kick in[/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/b8adbbc56509b25c15dae1f004b875b4d3b45ade.gif[/img]

Depending on which part of your brain got affected, you might either be [b]presented with a set of negative symptoms[/b] to choose from or [b]random parts from your adaptation tree will be burned out temporarily[/b]. There might even be a situation where your health will be lowered till the moment you finish a given challenge. Let’s focus for a while on the adaptation part, as I’ll come back to the symptoms later. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/a33cc521cb528f245f38cdd1ca7e981ac55d1238.gif[/img]

The way it works is simple – let’s assume that the first section got burned out, which means that in order to create an ax for example you’ll need three branches, four rocks, and two ropes, instead of two rocks, one branch, and one rope. If you want to pull everything back to the normal state, you’ll have to complete the given challenge – [b]from walking 5,000 steps, to killing two random animals[/b], and so on.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/1de6c363513256cdd5fc8623bbf52bff8efe9a7a.gif[/img]

[h2]Symptoms 🤒[/h2]

Now, let’s talk a little bit more about symptoms in Winter Survival. For those of you who have previously played our prologue, you know that those might make your blood boil. However, since the prologue release, we’ve been working tirelessly on some brand-new symptoms as well as improving the old ones. Let’s start with the coimetrophobia 😱

[h3]Coimetrophobia☠️[/h3]

Simply put – fear of the graves. If you’ve already played our demo (if not, I highly encourage you to do so) you might have noticed that there are quite a lot of graves scattered around the area. What this symptom does is every time you’re close to a grave you’ll slowly run out of stamina. The closer you get, the faster your stamina will deplete. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/bfe4d8f4ee442e43e46293b217dad642c914b4a1.gif[/img]

[h3]Delusional predator 🐺[/h3]

If you thought that wolves are gonna be your pain in the butt (I mean, they will be eventually) what do you think about phantom ones? Yes, that’s right – if you decide to go with the delusional predator symptom, sooner or later you’ll start seeing fake wolves scattered around the map. Don’t worry tho – if you take a closer look, they slightly differ from the normal ones. How cool is that? 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/b341171f5b3d1a96b4c6f3211a24389e134eab4c.gif[/img]

[h3]Delusional prey 🦌[/h3] 

Apart from the delusional predator symptom, we’ve also managed to add the prey as well. From now on, you’ll be hunted (pun intended) by phantom deers and rabbits during your voyage and fight for a tiny piece of meat. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/87987e756dfb100e54a73d9e4733ef79edeaa75c.gif[/img]

[h2]Languages[/h2]

With the demo being available on the Steam Next Fest, we've also managed to add a bunch of heavily requested languages. From now on you can play Winter Survival demo in your mother tounge – how cool is that? 

[h2]Stay up-to-date 📰[/h2]

Phew…That’s a long devlog, isn’t it? I can already say that it’s just the beginning as we’ll have the second part for you ready by this Friday. Anyway, let me know down in the comments how you like this devlog and if you have any suggestions regarding the future devlogs and game itself, make sure to leave your feedback in the comments down below. Last but not the least, if you feel like Winter Survival is your cup of tea, check the demo which is currently available as a part of Steam Next Fest, and add the game to your wishlist, so you won’t miss the [b]Early Access release on February 28th, 2024![/b] 🙇

[i]~Your humble marketing guy - Sewek[/i]

notes.title: Easier wolves, improved tutorials, and bug fixes – Demo Update #1 ⚒️
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/0246e802c4ace7935a6a1602fbe5500c9ae80a73.jpg[/img]
[h1]Hey, survivors! ❄️[/h1]

It’s been three days already since we’ve released our brand-new demo, and we’re so thankful for the amount of constructive feedback we’ve gathered so far from you. Without your support, we wouldn’t be able to track those pesky bugs & issues, and bring the solution to you as fast as we can. 

Today, I’d like to announce that we’ve already implemented most of your feedback into the demo. This means easier wolves on explorer difficulty, improved tutorial system, more hiding bushes and healing materials, and so on. Full patch notes are available down below 👇

[h2]Patch Notes: 7810[/h2]

[h3]General:[/h3]
[list]
[*]Wolves should now again grant experience when killed.
[*]Disorder hits perks now properly and applies negative perks.
[*]DLSS no longer breaks when loading or changing level.
[*]You should no longer get stuck if Wolf attacks you while you are solving the padlock puzzle.
[*]HDR options removed as they were not working correctly. Will likely bring them back in future once we can apply fixes. (You might need to reset your configs if you previously played with HDR options).
[*]Added Hunting Station and craftable spear recipe to starting shelter in Sickness scenario.
[*]Fixed issues related to wolf attacks when two different wolf attacks occuring fast one after another, would cause loss of input.
[*]More eating animations added (will add option to allow skipping of these in Difficulty settings in the future.)
[*]Dollar Coins can now stack.
[*]Fixed issue where you could hit yourself with the spear and have it break or get stuck unexpectedly.
[*]Many sound effect tweaks.
[/list]

[h3]Localizations:[/h3]
[list]
[*]Spanish added. (There might be some translations still missing - we are using it as a test before adding more.)
[/list]

[h3]Tutorials:[/h3]
[list]
[*]Tutorials should be more reliably repeatable in "How To Play" section.
[*]Tutorials have been tweaked based on feedback to make impaling and torch sections a little clearer.
[*]Minor tweaks to digging section.
[/list]

[h3]Balance:[/h3]
[list]
[*]Bleeding damage left by Wolf on the player reduced by 60% on all difficulties.
[*]Added few bandages and spears for explorers to find.
[*]Crow detection boxes increased so its easier to hit them with rocks or snowballs.
[*]Set that perception fatigue has 5% chance to trigger (same as on Survivalist difficulty) was on 2.5% before.
[*]Reduced the total amount of wolves on the map slightly to make it less dangerous on all difficulties.
[*]Tweaked the rates that Wolves 'forget' the player, allowing players to 'lose' wolves by hiding in bushes while in combat and sneaking around the bush while wolf searches for them in their last 'seen' location. (Generally we want to make getting into combat with wolves more avoidable and allow for more options other than running or fighting.)
[*]Added chance for Fiber to be collected from Tall Grass, as an alternative to more lucrative berry bushes in order to be able to craft bandages a bit more easily.
[*]Makeshift syrup will now also heal you for 100 health on top of delaying the RRI Effect.
[*]On "Explorer" (easy) difficulty impaling is now automatic as long as you are charging the spear and roughly aiming at the wolf when he jumps at you. (We are working on a custom difficulty options where you can tweak all options individually to your liking but it will likely not be before release of early access).
[*]Tweaked energy losses for the demo, so we lose energy faster (more sleeping required).
[/list]
[h3]Animals:[/h3]
[list]
[*]Animals should no longer see us through buildings.
[*]Animals should no longer hear us when crouched which should allow sneaking in wild and hiding in the bushes to be much more effective (we are still tweaking this further so that you can't walk all the way up to deer in future fixes).
[*]Minor rotation adjustment tweaks to wolf movement that should make them spin in circles less often.
[*]Boars should now be properly skinnable.
[/list]
[h3]Visuals:[/h3]
[list]
[*]Tweaked many places to raise the visual quality (mainly noticable in shelter and hot springs in the sickness scenario)
[*]Work on visuals is ongoing and will continue until early access release and further :) 
[*]Reduced flashlight intensity as it was too intense and whitened everything.
[*]Several minor graphical tweaks to raise the quality a little (higher texture sizes on terrain, RVT's etc.)
[*]Noise/Smearing artifact effects removed from Grass and other foliage.
[*]Noise/Smearing artifact effects removed from River.
[*]Refactoring of color grading based on players feedback
[*]Increased view distance on clear weathers
[/list]
[h3]Extra information that might be helpful:[/h3]
[list]
[*]Don't hold the button to swing torch, press and release - don't let the red bar disappear.
[/list]

[h3]Known issues at time of release:[/h3]
[list]
[*]Deer might be slow to notice us. (Due to crouching noise fixes).
[*]Fainting (getting to 0 energy) might lock up inputs and not play the fainting animation properly.
[*]When spear is in hand the Quick Actions Tab (bottom right corner) might wrongly show extra information for auto impaling / to release to impale regardless of difficulty.
[/list]

Apart from making the wolves easier on the explorer difficulty, we've also prepared for you a short video which should teach you how to fight with those pesky, furry friends. Keep in mind that from now on, releasing the spear before wolf jumps on you is only related to the survivalist difficulty. Let us know what you guys think! 

[previewyoutube=fsjU5yaBdD0;full][/previewyoutube]

[i]By the way – as you can see in the video, we also have some problems while fighting with them, so there is nothing to be worried about.[/i]

Oh... And one more thing – we clearly see that there is a little confusion about where to find our demo, since some of you might think that it's actually a prologue. 

You can freely download the demo from the Winter Survival's Steam page. It's definitely worth a try since it's a truly open world survival experience. Go and check it for yourself.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1394960/Winter_Survival/

Before we finish I'd like to invite all of you to our live stream on [b]February 6th, 2024 at 7 pm CET time[/b]. We'll be talking everything Winter Survival and we cannot wait to see you there. Feel free to ask any questions you might have – we'll do our best to answer them. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/fd60f1a983a10e9a8fb70ae7bb99ce4f1693f662.jpg[/img]

[i]~Your humble marketing guy – Sewek[/i]

notes.notes:
[h1]Hey, survivors![/h1]

Welcome back to another exciting devlog for Winter Survival. As we continue to shape our frozen wilderness, I’m thrilled to invite you to join me on a jaw-dropping adventure, where I’m gonna be sharing another part of our advanced mechanics series. If you somehow missed the first part, you can still check it out right now by clicking this link. In today’s devlog, I’ll delve into some intricate interactions with the local fauna, highlighting the intelligence and unpredictability of the animals that roam our wintry landscapes. Without further ado, let’s jump straight into the devlog. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/72aad1036448bd1cbfdcf9e4f9419d7b2cfb4270.png[/img]

[h2]Advanced Mechanics 🧠[/h2]

[h3]Wolf Party 🐺[/h3]

One of the most intriguing dynamics in Winter Survival is the emergence of wolf parties. Picture this: as you navigate the snow-covered environment, you may stumble upon a group of wolves feasting on a fresh carcass. These wolf parties add a layer of unpredictability to your survival journey. Now it’s for you to decide, because it’s a high risk but high reward thing – if you have a torch, you can always try to fend them off and take what’s left from the carcass. Whether you’re gonna be successful or not by doing so depends on your survival skills and how well you’re prepared. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/e8390f0c814c70f1294116b29a6c9a42258fb0ca.gif[/img]

[h3]Wounded Animal 🦌[/h3]

Another awe-inspiring feature that our team has implemented is the wounded animal as we like to call it. Just like in real world, the environment reacts to certain activities that we do on a daily basis. In Winter Survival it's basically the same case. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/1d81fe3d49508c3f011b0d6bf988c19dbab85d2d.gif[/img]

If you happen to trap and hurt a deer, you have a small window of opportunity to hunt it down and take as much as you can. You never know if there aren't any wolves nearby.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/06c0febaff6ffbf5338b5cf96dd335f609623bbd.gif[/img]

[h3]Bear Rampage 🐻[/h3]

Surviving the winter isn't just about battling the elements and hunger; it's also about navigating the animal threats, especially the bear. In Winter Survival, we've introduced a heavily impactful mechanic where our dreaded nemesis can inadvertently destroy player-built shelters. 

Let me give you an example – let’s assume that you’re going out into the wilderness in search of supplies, crafting materials, or just to explore the surrounding area. By the time you come back you might find that your cozy shelter is partially destroyed. Now the question is – Are you gonna risk your life and stay in the area? Or maybe you decide to leave this place and your belongings behind for a while and come back as soon as you feel like the area is secured? Let me tell ya – I’d make the decision sooner rather than later, because our furry friend might be back in the blink of an eye. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/5c90ff373d153093d0ac1f73424dca7410cacbd3.jpg[/img]

[h2]Stay up-to-date 📰[/h2]

As we wrap up this devlog, we're thrilled to showcase the depth and complexity of Winter Survival's game world. The wolf parties, wolf howls, and bear rampages are just a glimpse into the intricate tapestry we're weaving for players. Every playthrough promises a fresh set of challenges and surprises, thanks to the advanced mechanics that make our world truly dynamic and alive.

Before we finish, I’d also like to mention that our friends over at Pyramid Games would like to invite you to check what they’ve been cooking up for their jaw-dropping, set on a Mars survival game - Occupy Mars. The best thing though – the game is currently on sale, so if you’re looking for scientific-oriented survival game, or maybe you’d like to give it to someone special, Occupy Mars will definitely meet your expectations

https://store.steampowered.com/app/758690/Occupy_Mars_The_Game/

And that’s gonna be it for today! Stay tuned for more updates as we continue to refine and expand Winter Survival. I can't wait for you to experience the peril and beauty of our frozen realm. Until next time, stay warm, stay vigilant, and may your survival instincts guide you through the winter's unforgiving embrace. Until the next devlog!

notes.title: Winter Survival Development Update #15 – Advanced Mechanics part 1 ⚒️
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/310f49a9a27e2847f16198746c8e902597b49744.jpg[/img]
[h1]Hey, survivors! ❄️[/h1]

Welcome to another Winter Survival’s development update. In our recent announcement I’ve delved deeper into everything bear-related, so if you haven’t read it yet, you can freely do so by clicking [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1394960/view/6738003788162098620]this link[/url]. 

So, what do I have for you today? In today’s devlog we’re gonna dive into more advanced game mechanics – some of those are connected strictly to survival, and some exist to show you the effects of your actions to stay alive, often at any cost. Grab your favorite drink, prepare some snacks, and let’s roll! 

[h2]Sleeping outside 🛌[/h2]

Let’s start with the simplest yet most common mechanic – sleeping outside. In most survival games what you’d normally do is to build a basic shelter where you can sleep and save your progress. Then you’d venture deeper into the world in search of the perfect spot on the map where you’d start building your dream base a.k.a. recreating Minas Tirith or something else. 

In Winter Survival it’s “just” a little bit different – technically you can sleep outside. However, it can lead to some unexpected consequences. First one being the drop of your body temperature assuming that you didn’t make a fire. Even if you did take care of that, there is another thing – unforeseen wolf encounters, as I like to call it. If you have a torch at hand or even a spear then you might be able to fend them off, but if not… Then let me tell ya – the future doesn’t seem so bright for you. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/b67124eb789c0abb010dc6ab1820f14e9c8351d1.gif[/img]

[h2]Cooking outside 🍖[/h2]

“I’m starving, so I’m just gonna make a campfire and cook some delicious meat that I stole from the unexpected nightly pack of wolves. It won’t take that much time, so soon my stomach is gonna be full, and I’ll be ready for another day” – thought one already dead survivalist. 

In other words – I highly advise you to think twice before you’ll make the choice to cook outside as the smell will attract wild animals. If you’re lucky enough you’ll encounter a boar, but what if that’s gonna be a bear? Let me give you some advice – cooking outside is a last resort, and you’ll need to think twice before you make the decision. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/654a9b76d96261050426e764a01d1f5a4238e279.gif[/img]

[h2]Stench 🦨[/h2]

Just like in real life, doing certain actions will make your character sweat, which will lead to you building up quite a stench. But how is that supposed to be a problem? You might think. Well, the answer is simple – animal noses are far more sensitive than our human ones. Hunting will become a problem as the animals will smell you from a mile away. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/98c5e80f20fca153f6bc625cff8a4e58e42f550e.gif[/img]

As you can see, hunting takes time and proper preparation, so if you want to avoid being spotted before you even notice your prey, washing yourself before will do the trick. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/f5e7296ec5eac58f22c720e1355e5916fe819c36.gif[/img]

[h2]Cargo 📦[/h2]

Surprise, surprise… It’s a special delivery time. From time to time, a plane will drop a cargo box in a random place on the map. The box will contain some high-value resources, so it’s definitely something worth venturing out for. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/2ff3244ef6ac57ec46d64ef7361097add6c1d64a.jpg[/img]

However, it won’t be that easy. Not only will the cargo drop in the evening, when there’s gonna be a bunch of wild animals lurking in the shadows, but also you’ll have a limited time to get the resources you want. To find the exact location of a cargo, you’re gonna need to use your walkie-talkie. Think of it as a hot & cold game – the closer you’ll get to the cargo location, the stronger the signal will be from the walkie-talkie. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/4daa6012e6e4c38ad8988e4d76a526a6e93c985e.gif[/img]

[h2]Stay up-to-date 📰[/h2]

And this is how this devlog comes to an end. What do you think about some of the advanced mechanics that you will encounter in the game? Did you enjoy today’s devlog? Make sure to let us know in the comments below. However, please do keep in mind that it's still work-in-progress stuff, so some things that you've witnessed here might differ from the final product. Last but not the least, if you don’t want to miss the next devlog or any other news regarding Winter Survival, consider adding the game to your wishlist 🙇

notes.title: Winter Survival devlog #14 – The Bear 🐻
notes.notes:
[b][h1]Hey, survivors![/h1][/b]

Welcome to another development update for Winter Survival. As you might already know, [b]Winter Survival is set to launch on February 28th, 2024[/b]. For more details, check out our recent announcement [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1394960/view/3717214241902031531]here[/url]. 

In today’s devlog I’m gonna delve into the matter of the dreaded nemesis that will make surviving in the harsh environment even harder – The Bear. I’m gonna cover everything from the initial concept and ideas to its current state and role in the game. Make sure to grab your favorite drink and join me on this journey. Not gonna lie – I’ve gotta hurry up, cause I can already feel his presence around 😱

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/cc9262205f76da20676b049c18c083e5041e8ff4.jpg[/img]

[h2]How did it all begin?[/h2]

Since the start of this project, we already knew that we wanted to make a game that will be different from other survival games. On the one hand, we still wanted to keep the core elements of the survival genre. On the other hand, we wanted to give you a challenging experience that will constantly put your survival skills to the test. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/af38f204fa35d4a41718dc93cf31ecb819acd740.gif[/img]

This is where the bear comes into play, as you will be able to feel his presence most of the time in the wilderness. Additionally, he is an apex predator and even a well crafted spear won’t be enough to deal with him. More on that later on. 

[h2]How the bear’s changed over the time[/h2]

If you’ve paid close attention on our social media channels, you might have realized one specific video focusing on our furry friend (note: he is not friendly at all). As I understand that you might still be busy playing all those wonderful games that have been released recently, I thought that it would be nice to share this video once again, but this time here with ya, folks! Not gonna lie – our bear has definitely been through some rough times. What do you think about one who will be hunting not only your body, but mind as well? Make sure to leave your answers in the comments.

[previewyoutube=73bAxG9yeoE;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]How does the bear actually work?[/h2]

In this section I’d like to delve into all of the details regarding the bear’s behavior. I will divide it into separate categories as the bear behavior changes depending on which game mode you chose to play. Let’s start with the Story Mode, so sit down folks, and let me tell you a tale. 

[h3]Story Mode[/h3]

In the Story Mode the bear will play a significant role as it’ll be constantly following your and your friends’ trail. Your success highly depends on whether you will be able to avoid/sneak past his presence or not. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/dd5bba5842e7b2763474a35335ea6c02406fee10.png[/img]

[h3]Endless Mode[/h3]

In the Endless Mode his role drastically changes. While you’ll be exploring the area for additional supplies and materials, you’ll be able to spot his trail over a certain period of time. After that, you’ll be given a little bit of time to prepare some sort of decoy to get rid of the bear for a while. However, if you happen to fail fulfilling that task, the bear will spawn within a random place in the area that you’re currently settled in and will start patrolling the region. 

Now, you’re probably wondering – How do I get rid of the bear then? Well, the answer is simple yet quite challenging – if you want the bear to stop being a pain in the butt, you’ll need to venture to a different region until our furry comrade decides to leave you in peace. You can still prepare a meat pile for him, but you’ll need to figure out how to approach him without being spotted. 

[h2]Broken shelters[/h2]

What do you think about going on a trip down the memory lane? As you might remember from one of our devlogs, your shelter will be vulnerable not only to the dynamically changing weather but also to wild animals attacks. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/98389ce955e95f6a5eb14aeedb12acd2050e8241.png[/img]

In other words – if you thought that venturing into the wilderness and leaving your shelter unprotected was a good idea, then my friend, you were wrong! Just check out these shelters – next time you leave your door open it’ll be even worse. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/b9c23216a8252e079bb65d54c040a5b43720f839.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38695406/ef146b59341a35de5523a91135a51fdc065176f3.png[/img]

Phew…I’ve found myself a nice, cozy spot to hide from the bear for a while, so before he finds me I’d like to bid you farewell.
